page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.2xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual server configured with integrated high-speed local instance storage and enhanced networking capabilities. Compute is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz across 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with dedicated allocation. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and features support for AVX-512 instructions, including AVX-512 VNNI. System memory totals 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes a bundled 300 GB local NVMe SSD and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no attached GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent middle-tier throughput for multi-threaded and memory-bound operations, contrasted by modest single-threaded compute capacity. The server recorded 6,753.03 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 7,659.89, both ranking in the middle tier. Memory subsystem testing demonstrates 49.28 GB/sec in large-block read throughput and 37.44 GB/sec in write throughput. In transactional benchmarks, it sustained 6.43 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 2,710.98 in PassMark database testing. In contrast, single-thread compute metrics such as Geekbench single-core (1123.0) and compression utilities ranked in the lower tiers, reflecting the older microarchitecture of the Xeon Cascade Lake generation.

Because the server combines balanced compute-to-memory density with low-latency local NVMe storage and 8 Gbps networking, it is well aligned with workloads requiring quick scratch disk access alongside standard resource allocations. Appropriate deployment targets include caching layers like Redis or Memcached, transactional relational databases needing temporary storage, continuous integration build nodes, and general enterprise backend applications. Workloads that depend heavily on single-thread instruction throughput or modern accelerated matrix computation may encounter bottlenecks.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Built on the AWS Nitro system, this configuration bundles a 300 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed scratch space and delivers an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results show average multi-core and memory subsystem throughput, including 6.43 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 49.28 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth, alongside weaker single-threaded performance metrics. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio and low-latency ephemeral storage, the m5dn.2xlarge is technically appropriate for mid-tier relational databases, caching layers, application backend servers, and compilation jobs requiring local NVMe I/O.
